title: Identity Exposure Assurance
ogQuestion: Do access controls still enforce what policy says?
intent: Commercial: continuing proof that identity controls enforce the intended access
brief: Identity policy decays through exclusions, guests, dormant accounts and application grants. Covers effective enforcement coverage, exclusion growth, dormant identity age, authentication strength and non-human identities.

title: Privileged Access Assurance
ogQuestion: Is every standing privilege still justified today?
intent: Commercial: continuing proof that privileged access is minimal, time-bound and reviewed
brief: Privilege accumulates and is rarely removed. Covers standing versus eligible assignment, elevation evidence, emergency account governance, review quality and privileged non-human identities.

title: Cloud Security Exposure Assurance
ogQuestion: Which exposures are reachable right now?
intent: Commercial: continuing proof of cloud exposure position, prioritised by reachability
brief: Posture tools list findings; assurance holds a threshold on reachable exposure and its age. Covers public exposure, attack-path reachability, configuration regression and ownership of each open exposure.

title: Vulnerability Remediation Assurance
ogQuestion: Was the fix verified, or only the ticket closed?
intent: Commercial: remediation owned through to verified closure
brief: Closure is a re-test result, not a ticket status. Covers exploitation-informed prioritisation, remediation time against agreed windows, re-test evidence, regression after rebuild and exception expiry. Canonical page for security remediation.

title: Secrets Exposure Assurance
ogQuestion: Is every credential known, scoped, rotated and unexposed?
intent: Commercial: continuing proof that credentials are inventoried, rotated and not exposed
brief: Secrets spread into repositories, pipelines, images and AI tool configuration. Covers inventory, age against rotation policy, exposure detection to revocation time, and replacement of long-lived credentials with federated identity.
